newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SHORT BUT RATES STEADY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SHORT BUT RATES STEADY.

text.p: Zimbabwe's short-term trading rates were quoted largely stable on Tuesday despite a shortage of cash in the system, dealers said.

"The market was Z$158.9 million short on Monday and the central bank forecast a shortage of Z$46 million for today," one dealer said, adding that the Reserve Bank did not auction any treasury bills as was the norm to mop up excess liquidity.
He said the shortage was caused mainly by foreign currency payments that had drained money off the local money market.
On Tuesday, treasury bills were being sold on the secondary market unchanged from Monday's 24.75 percent and call money was also stable at 22 percent.
NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 26.5 percent, slightly down from 26.6 percent but sold at a steady 25.5 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills were stable at 25.5 percent (buying) and at 24.75 percent (selling).
